# `modules/EditorParticles.js`

> **Source:** `editor/js/modules/EditorParticles.js`

EditorParticles - Particle system integration for the editor Wraps the engine's ParticleSimWorld and ParticleBillboardRenderer to provide real-time particle preview in the editor viewport.

### `createComposedSpellEffect(editor, sourceEntityId, elements, baseConfig)`

=== AUTO-BLENDING SPELL EFFECT COMPOSER === Applies composed spell effect properties directly to the source emitter. Does NOT create child entities — modifies the source emitter's visual properties based on the element mix to produce a richer, more layered look. The composer analyzes the element combination and applies: - Optimized color derived from element combo - Adjusted emit rate, size, lifetime for a "spell-like" feel - Temperature and material properties from element chemistry Called by "Create Spell From This" button in EmitterInspectorCard.js.

**Parameters:**

- `editor` *(Object)* — Editor instance
- `sourceEntityId` *(number)* — Entity ID of the source emitter
- `elements` *(Array)* — Active element layers [{id, power, enabled}]
- `baseConfig` *(Object)* — Base emitter config (rate, size, lifetime, etc.)

**Returns:** True if spell properties were applied

### `spawnDustPuff(position, color, intensity = 0.5, normal)`

Spawn a dust puff at a world position when fragments take damage or break. Uses small, soft point particles colored to match the breaking material. Best-practice references (real-time VFX): - Unreal Niagara: one-shot burst, soft sprite, high drag, gravity settle - Unity VFX Graph: short lifetime, size-over-life bell curve, alpha fade - GDC "The Art of Destruction": dust = desaturated material color, 0.2-0.6s

**Parameters:**

- `position` *(number[])* — — [x,y,z] world-space contact point
- `color` *(number[])* — — [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a] material base color (0-1)
- `intensity` *(number)* — — 0-1 scale (maps to particle count + spread)
- `[normal]` *(number[])* — — optional impact normal for directional puff

## Notes & Examples

### Editor Extension System

The editor supports extensions via the same Plauna component system as apps. Extensions can add panels, tools, menu items, and hooks into the engine. They run with elevated 'editor' capability granting access to the scene graph, asset database, and build pipeline.

**Example: Editor extension adding a custom panel**
```js
import { Extension } from 'editor/core/Extension.js';
import { Panel } from 'editor/ui/Panel.js';

class TerrainEditor extends Extension {
  id = 'terrain-editor';
  capabilities = ['editor', 'scene'];
  
  activate(context) {
    // Add menu item
    context.menus.add('Tools/Terrain', () => this.open());
    
    // Register tool
    context.tools.register('terrain', {
      icon: 'mountain',
      onSelect: (entity) => this.edit(entity)
    });
  }
  
  open() {
    this.panel = new Panel({
      title: 'Terrain Editor',
      content: this.buildUI()
    });
    context.workspace.addPanel(this.panel);
  }
  
  edit(entity) {
    const terrain = entity.get(TerrainComponent);
    this.panel.bind(terrain);
  }
}

editor.extensions.register(TerrainEditor);
```

**See also:** [Editor Overview](/editor/overview.md)
